approach: Differentiate the position equation to get velocity, differentiate again to get acceleration, then apply the conditions asked.

steps.text: Write the velocity and acceleration by differentiating x with respect to time.
steps.equation: x = 20 + t³ − 12t, v = dx/dt = 3t² − 12, a = dv/dt = 6t

steps.text: Substitute t = 0 into x and v.

steps.why_this_step: Uniformly accelerated motion needs a constant acceleration; here a depends on t, so it is not.

steps.text: Set v = 0 and solve for t.
steps.equation: 3t² − 12 = 0 → t² = 4 → t = 2 s (t = −2 s rejected, time cannot be negative)

steps.text: Substitute t = 2 s into x to get the position where velocity is zero.

final_answer.value: (a) x(0) = 20 m, v(0) = −12 m/s; (b) not uniformly accelerated, since a = 6t is not constant; (c) x = 4 m when v = 0

common_mistakes.text: Taking both roots t = 2 s and t = −2 s as valid positions gives an extra wrong answer x(−2) = 36 m for a time before the motion starts.
Assuming acceleration is constant just because it comes from a smooth equation leads to wrongly calling the motion uniformly accelerated.
